title: Resource Exhaustion and Asynchronous Traps
platform_conditions: .NET Framework 4.x and modern .NET; Regex match timeout is opt-in per instance or app-domain wide
security_mechanism: The .NET regex engine backtracks without any internal time limit unless a timeout is supplied, so one crafted subject against a nested-quantifier pattern pins a CPU core indefinitely inside Match/IsMatch/Replace. Unbounded request bodies and collection growth allocate server memory until OOM; async void methods route exceptions to the synchronously-invoked context where they crash the process unobserved; and C# defaults to unchecked integer arithmetic, so an overflow silently wraps a length or limit to a small value that then passes a downstream bounds check.

source_sink_clues.source: Request bodies, query-string values fed to regexes, uploaded collections, and arithmetic operands derived from request-declared sizes.
source_sink_clues.sink: Regex.Match/IsMatch/Replace on instances without a matchTimeout; reads and collections grown from request data with no cap; async void handlers on request paths; checked-arithmetic-free comparisons guarding sizes

tracking_guards: Require Regex instances over untrusted input to carry a timeout (the TimeSpan constructor overload or Regex.MatchTimeout app-wide setting); require body/length caps before parsing; require async Task instead of async void on request handlers; require checked arithmetic or explicit range checks on security-relevant sizes.
not_candidate_when: The pattern is a constant without nested quantifiers and the subject is length-capped, the regex carries an explicit match timeout, request size limits are enforced by the platform before the code runs, or the async void is a UI event handler outside request processing.
synthetic_safe_example: Regex reg = new Regex(pattern, RegexOptions.None, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1));
